question.text: What must a Regulated Entity do as part of ongoing sanctions screening under the IFSCA Guidelines?

answer.text: Review customers, their business, and transactions against UN Security Council sanctions lists and other relevant sanctions lists
Screen only new customers at the time of onboarding
Screen only against domestic sanctions lists published by the Government of India
Screen only high-risk customers against international sanctions lists

explanation.text: The Logic: As part of ongoing customer due diligence, a Regulated Entity must review its customers, their business and their transactions against the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) sanctions lists and any other relevant sanctions lists. This is a continuing obligation that applies throughout the business relationship, not just at onboarding. The Trap: Screening only new customers, only against domestic lists, or only high-risk customers each falls short of the IFSCA ongoing-screening requirement, which applies to ALL customers, against BOTH UNSC and other relevant lists, on a CONTINUOUS basis. Note: The immediate blocking / freezing-and-reporting obligation in the workbook is specifically tied to a wire-transfer name-screening hit against terrorist designations; the general ongoing sanctions-screening clause requires the Regulated Entity to act in accordance with the applicable sanctions framework and report account matches (for example, to FIU-IND and the Ministry of Home Affairs).
